project: SP-002 Round 1: Universal Confounder Stress Test for Bio-AI
scientific_question: Can a model-agnostic audit score, computed from dependence, cohort shift, missingness reliance, prevalence sensitivity, subgroup instability, calibration drift, and feature shift, identify biomedical ML configurations whose naive validation materially overstates rigorous generalization?

domains.rigorous_evaluation: patient-grouped outer evaluation plus forward encounter-order stress test

domains.license: CC BY 4.0 archive; source studies cited individually
domains.rigorous_evaluation: leave-one-study-out on gene-symbol-collapsed common features; all selection/scaling/imputation learned in training studies
domains.naive_evaluation: pooled stratified random split ignoring study
domains.invalid_diagnostic_arm: pooled preprocessing/harmonization before split, labeled leakage demonstration only

exclusions: motor_UPDRS from predictors due direct target overlap

audit_dimensions.dependence_leakage: overlap or similarity between train and evaluation units; repeated-unit detectability
audit_dimensions.missingness_reliance: performance and permutation reliance on missingness indicators plus shifted-missingness stress
audit_dimensions.prevalence_sensitivity: metric/calibration change under fixed label-prevalence resampling grids
audit_dimensions.subgroup_instability: worst-group minus overall performance for prespecified demographic/clinical groups with adequate n
audit_dimensions.calibration_drift: absolute calibration slope/intercept and Brier/MAE change
audit_dimensions.feature_shift: train-test multivariate shift summarized from univariate standardized distances and classifier two-sample test

audit_score: Before evaluation, each dimension is min-max clipped to [0,1] using prespecified physical/statistical bounds in code; composite is their unweighted mean. Missing dimensions are reported and composite is not issued unless >=5/7 dimensions exist.
primary_outcome: configuration-level optimism delta: naive validation performance minus rigorous external/group-aware performance; AUROC scale for classification, normalized RMSE improvement scale for regression
material_optimism: delta >= 0.05 on the domain-normalized performance scale
evaluation_design: Configurations are the objects of evaluation. Outer leave-one-domain-out calibration: score thresholds and any dimension bounds not physically fixed are learned on two domains and evaluated on the third. No evaluation configuration contributes to threshold fitting.
success_gate_all_required: Across configurations, audit score Spearman rho with optimism delta >=0.60 and cluster-bootstrap 95% lower bound >0, clustering by domain and resampling independent units within domains
At least two of three domains show naive-versus-rigorous optimism delta >=0.05 with Holm-adjusted p<0.05 for at least one nontrivial model configuration
Leave-one-domain-out fixed-threshold detection of material optimism has sensitivity >=0.80 and specificity >=0.60 pooled across held-out domains
Full composite detector AUROC exceeds every single-dimension audit detector and every leave-one-dimension-out ablation by >=0.02 on average under leave-one-domain-out evaluation
All negative controls pass: shuffled labels produce no above-chance rigorous model performance; random group labels do not create systematic optimism; valid pipelines have zero detected unit overlap
A clean rerun reproduces every gate metric within absolute tolerance 1e-8 or documented deterministic-library tolerance <=1e-6
negative_controls: duplicate-row injection positive test for detector

statistics.uncertainty: cluster/bootstrap at the domain-appropriate unit with 5000 replicates for final gates
statistics.multiple_testing: Holm adjustment across primary domain/model contrasts
statistics.reporting: effect sizes and confidence intervals mandatory; no gate by p-value alone

failure_policy: Failure of any required success criterion makes Round 1 a negative result. Preserve all outputs and use them to select Round 2; no success paper.
environment_requirements: Pin Python/R and all scientific package versions; record commands, database/archive checksums, CPU/RAM/time ceilings. Use scikit-learn, pandas, numpy, scipy, R/Biobase and mature open tooling rather than hand-rolled estimators.
commercial_product_test: Separately evaluate a CLI/report generator for deterministic schema, corrupt-input rejection, missing-dimension behavior, runtime, memory, audit trace, and human-readable evidence dossier. Product acceptance cannot rescue a failed scientific gate.
